subject: Renewal Options — BrightEdge term structure & staggered-commit proposals
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Morales <sasha.morales@brightedge.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal options — BrightEdge term structure & staggered-commit proposals

Hi Sasha,

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per Tomia’s request I pulled together three structured options for BrightEdge’s 2027 renewal that are intended to address procurement’s co-term preference, your team’s desire for predictable unit economics while scaling capacity through the year, and the auto-renew behavior you mentioned. I’ve attached a draft SOW and a pricing grid (staggered schedule).

High level — three options (summary):

- Option A — 12-month co-term (co-term to 12/31/2027), single invoice, 15% multi-year discount applied if you convert to a 2-year commitment by signing before 12/15.
- Option B — Staggered-commit schedule (recommended): upfront commit for Q1 capacity, two scheduled ramp increases (start of Q2 and Q4). Co-term to 12/31/2027, monthly invoice, prorated invoicing on each ramp. Includes 10% ramp-credit on incremental units in Q2 and Q4 to smooth budget impact.
- Option C — Multi-year 24-month fixed commit with 18% discount and guaranteed baseline capacity across both years; annual true-up.

Key details in the attachments: pricing_grid_staggered.xlsx has per-token unit price at each commit band and expected monthly invoices; BrightEdge_SOW_v3.pdf reflects the canary/rollout clause we discussed (automatic fallback to a lower-quant variant if capacity is constrained).

Ask: Could you confirm which option you want us to expand into a final SOW? Procurement also asked for proration rules and an explicit auto-renew toggle in the contract; I’ve sketched the language in the SOW (see Section 4). If we go with Option B I’ll loop finance and legal for the prorated monthly billing and the ramp credits.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 30-min call to walk through the grid.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: BrightEdge_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf), pricing_grid_staggered.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Sasha Morales <sasha.morales@brightedge.io>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Tomia Chen <tomia.chen@brightedge.io>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options — BrightEdge term structure & staggered-commit proposals

Monica — thanks for the clear options and the docs. Tomia and I reviewed with procurement this morning. A few notes:

- Procurement is firm on a 12/31 co-term (they want our contracts to align across vendors).
- They prefer a single agreement but are OK with staged billing if the contract language guarantees co-term and proration on ramps.
- Auto-renew: procurement will only sign if there is an explicit opt-in checkbox; they don’t want automatic renew unless we reiterate a 60-day renewal notice.
- The staggered schedule looks promising, but finance wants clarity on how ramp credits are applied (line-item vs invoice-level credit).

Small ask: can you show an example invoice for Option B (month 1 base + Q2 ramp proration + credit application) so our finance team can see how it nets out? If Option B is workable we’ll likely pick it, but Tomia wants the DocuSign-ready SOW and clear billing sample.

Appreciate it — S

Sasha Morales
Director, Cloud Platform
BrightEdge Analytics
sasha.morales@brightedge.io

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Morales <sasha.morales@brightedge.io>
Cc: Tomia Chen <tomia.chen@brightedge.io>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T08:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options — BrightEdge term structure & staggered-commit proposals

Sasha / Tomia — great, glad procurement is aligned on co-term. Below I’ve sketched the invoicing example and clarified credit handling for Option B. I also attached the pricing grid with the invoice mock-up on tab "InvoiceExample".

Invoice example (Option B) — month 1 (Jan)
- Base commit: 100M tokens @ $0.0012 = $120,000
- Q2 ramp effective 2027-04-01: additional 50M tokens ramped; charge in April pro-rated for days in April: prorated_charge = (50M tokens * $0.00105) * (days_active/30).
- Ramp credits: applied as invoice-level credit in the same invoice month as the ramp charge; Q2 ramp credit = 10% of incremental ramp charge for first 3 months after ramp (applied monthly).
- Example net for April (simplified): prorated_ramp_charge = $17,500; credit = $1,750; net_ramp = $15,750.

Other contract items I added to SOW:
- Auto-renew language: agreement renews for 12 months at then-current pricing unless BrightEdge provides 60 days notice to opt out. We’ve included an explicit "auto-renew opt-in" checkbox in the signature page for procurement to choose otherwise.
- Co-term: Agreement end-date set to 2027-12-31 with a true-up within 30 days of period end.
- Billing cadence: monthly invoices, Net 30 payment terms (we can support monthly invoicing with purchase order).

If this looks good I’ll: 1) update the SOW to include the sample invoice table, 2) create a DocuSign envelope (SOW + signature exhibit with the opt-in checkbox), 3) loop Rishi / Finance for the >10% deviation approval on the ramp-credit structure.

I’ll wait for your confirmation before generating the DocuSign link.

—Monica

Attachments: pricing_grid_staggered.xlsx (invoice example tab)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal options — BrightEdge — approval needed (ramp-credit > standard)

Team — forwarding BrightEdge’s preference for Option B (staggered-commit) and the proposed ramp-credit (10% on incremental units for two quarters). Key asks:

- Rishi: this is outside standard promotional credits — can you approve the ramp-credit structure (10% for first 3 months post-ramp) against BE-5143?
- Vivek: legal to confirm the auto-renew opt-in checkbox language and co-term clause are acceptable for our standard SOW.
- Marcus / Finance: procurement at BrightEdge wants monthly invoices and a PO. Will we accept monthly invoicing with a PO and Net 30 for this account?

I’ve attached the SOW and invoice mock-up. Monica, happy to sync offline with anyone if needed.

Thanks,
Neha
Senior Customer Success Manager

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal options — BrightEdge — approval needed (ramp-credit > standard)

Thanks Neha — reviewed the numbers and business case. Approve the 10% ramp-credit for the two ramp events (Q2 and Q4), capped at the incremental units outlined in the pricing grid. Please ensure the credit is applied as an invoice-level credit and appears as a separate line item. Finance (Marcus) to confirm monthly PO handling.

Deal notes for the record: deal_id BE-5143; expected ARR at contract start ~ $1.9M; anticipated adoption-led expansion to push ARR to ~ $2.6M over 12 months assuming both ramp events complete.

Rishi
Head of Revenue Operations
